q: In TRD-01, is the domestic economy an importer or exporter when the world price is $5?
options: The graph does not determine the trade direction
feedback: The $5 world price lies below the $7 autarky price, so domestic demand exceeds domestic supply and the country imports.

q: At the $5 world price in TRD-01, how many thousand avocados do domestic producers supply?
feedback: The world-price line intersects domestic supply at Q = 125 thousand.

q: At the $5 world price in TRD-01, how many thousand avocados do domestic consumers demand?
feedback: The world-price line intersects domestic demand at Q = 225 thousand.

q: Using TRD-01, how many thousand avocados are imported at the $5 world price?
feedback: Imports equal domestic consumption minus domestic production: 225 − 125 = 100 thousand.

q: Why does TRD-01 show imports when trade opens at Pw = $5?
options: The world price is below the domestic autarky price
The world price is above the domestic autarky price
Domestic supply exceeds domestic demand at $5
The world price equals the autarky price
feedback: A small country imports when the world price is below its no-trade equilibrium price.

q: Relative to autarky in TRD-01, how do domestic production and consumption change when trade opens at $5?
options: Production rises by 50 thousand and consumption falls by 50 thousand
Production falls by 50 thousand and consumption rises by 50 thousand
Both production and consumption rise by 100 thousand
Both production and consumption fall by 50 thousand
feedback: Autarky quantity is 175 thousand; at Pw = $5, Qs = 125 and Qd = 225.

q: Using the demand intercept and Pw = $5 in TRD-01, consumer surplus under free trade is:
feedback: Consumer surplus is 1/2 × (14 − 5) × 225 = 1,012.5 thousand dollars.

q: In TRD-01, domestic producer surplus falls from $612.5 thousand under autarky to $312.5 thousand under free trade. What is the producer loss?
feedback: Producer surplus falls by 612.5 − 312.5 = 300 thousand dollars.

q: Using TRD-01, consumers gain $400 thousand and producers lose $300 thousand when trade opens. What is the net national gain?
feedback: The consumer gain exceeds the producer loss by $100 thousand.

q: Which package correctly summarizes TRD-01 after opening to trade at Pw = $5?
options: Qd = 125 thousand, Qs = 225 thousand, exports = 100 thousand
Qd = 225 thousand, Qs = 125 thousand, imports = 100 thousand
Qd = 225 thousand, Qs = 175 thousand, imports = 50 thousand
feedback: At the world price, demand is 225 thousand and supply is 125 thousand, leaving 100 thousand imports.

q: TRD-01 implies a $400 thousand consumer gain and a $300 thousand producer loss from opening trade. Which welfare statement is correct?
options: Total surplus falls by $100 thousand because producers lose
Total surplus is unchanged because gains equal losses
Total surplus rises by $100 thousand even though producers lose
Only producer surplus matters for national welfare
feedback: The distribution changes, but the consumer gain exceeds the producer loss by $100 thousand.

q: Checkpoint: At Pw = $5 in TRD-01, what creates the 100-thousand-unit import quantity?
options: Qs of 225 thousand minus Qd of 125 thousand
Autarky quantity of 175 thousand minus Qs of 125 thousand
World price of $5 multiplied by Qd of 225 thousand
Qd of 225 thousand minus Qs of 125 thousand
feedback: Imports are the gap between domestic quantity demanded and domestic quantity supplied at the world price.

q: In TRD-02, is the domestic economy an importer or exporter when the world price is $10?
options: The graph does not determine the trade direction
feedback: The $10 world price lies above the $7 autarky price, so domestic production exceeds domestic consumption and the country exports.

q: At Pw = $10 in TRD-02, domestic consumers demand:
feedback: The world-price line intersects demand at Q = 100 thousand.

q: At Pw = $10 in TRD-02, domestic producers supply:
feedback: The world-price line intersects supply at Q = 250 thousand.

q: Using TRD-02, how many thousand avocados are exported at Pw = $10?
feedback: Exports equal domestic production minus domestic consumption: 250 − 100 = 150 thousand.

q: Why does TRD-02 show exports when trade opens at Pw = $10?
options: The world price is above the domestic autarky price
The world price is below the domestic autarky price
Domestic demand exceeds domestic supply at $10
The world price is fixed at the autarky price
feedback: A world price above the no-trade equilibrium price creates excess domestic supply for export.

q: Relative to autarky in TRD-02, how do domestic production and consumption change after trade opens at $10?
options: Production falls by 75 thousand and consumption rises by 75 thousand
Production rises by 75 thousand and consumption falls by 75 thousand
Both production and consumption rise by 150 thousand
feedback: Autarky quantity is 175 thousand; with trade, Qs = 250 and Qd = 100.

q: Using TRD-02, producer surplus at Pw = $10 is:
feedback: With a supply curve through the origin, producer surplus is 1/2 × $10 × 250 = $1,250 thousand.

q: In TRD-02, consumer surplus falls from $612.5 thousand under autarky to $200 thousand under free trade. What is the consumer loss?
feedback: The loss is 612.5 − 200 = 412.5 thousand dollars.

q: Using TRD-02, producers gain $637.5 thousand while consumers lose $412.5 thousand. What is the net national gain from trade?
feedback: The producer gain exceeds the consumer loss by $225 thousand.

q: Which package correctly summarizes TRD-02 at Pw = $10?
options: Qs = 100 thousand, Qd = 250 thousand, imports = 150 thousand
Qs = 250 thousand, Qd = 100 thousand, exports = 150 thousand
Qs = Qd = 175 thousand, so exports are zero
Qs = 250 thousand, Qd = 175 thousand, exports = 75 thousand
feedback: At Pw = $10, domestic supply is 250 thousand and demand is 100 thousand, producing 150 thousand exports.

q: What distributional pattern does TRD-02 illustrate when an exporting market opens to trade?
options: Domestic consumers gain while producers lose, with a positive net gain
Both consumers and producers lose because domestic price rises
Domestic producers gain while domestic consumers lose, with a positive net gain
Only foreign buyers gain because exports leave the country
feedback: The higher world price benefits domestic sellers and hurts domestic buyers, while aggregate surplus rises.

q: Checkpoint: At Pw = $10 in TRD-02, how is the 150-thousand-unit export quantity calculated?
options: Qd of 250 thousand minus Qs of 100 thousand
Autarky quantity of 175 thousand minus Qd of 100 thousand
Pw of $10 multiplied by Qs of 250 thousand
Qs of 250 thousand minus Qd of 100 thousand
feedback: Exports are the excess of domestic quantity supplied over domestic quantity demanded at the world price.

q: In TRD-03, what domestic price results from the $4 world price plus the tariff?
feedback: The graph marks the tariff-inclusive domestic price at $6.

q: What is the per-unit tariff shown in TRD-03?
feedback: The domestic price rises from the $4 world price to $6, so the tariff is $2 per unit.

q: At the tariff-inclusive price of $6 in TRD-03, domestic production is:
feedback: The $6 line intersects domestic supply at Q = 100 thousand.

q: At the tariff-inclusive price of $6 in TRD-03, domestic consumption is:
feedback: The $6 line intersects demand at Q = 200 thousand.

q: After the tariff in TRD-03, imports equal:
feedback: At $6, Qd = 200 thousand and Qs = 100 thousand, so imports are 100 thousand.

q: Compared with free trade at Pw = $4, the tariff in TRD-03 reduces imports by:
feedback: Free-trade imports are 250 − 50 = 200 thousand; after the tariff they are 100 thousand.

q: Because quantities are measured in thousands, government tariff revenue in TRD-03 is:
feedback: The tariff is $2 on 100 thousand imports, so revenue is $200 thousand.

q: The tariff raises domestic production from 50 thousand to 100 thousand. What is the production-distortion loss in TRD-03?
feedback: The production triangle is 1/2 × $2 × 50 thousand = $50 thousand.

q: The tariff reduces domestic consumption from 250 thousand to 200 thousand. What is the consumption-distortion loss in TRD-03?
feedback: The consumption triangle is 1/2 × $2 × 50 thousand = $50 thousand.

q: What is the total deadweight loss created by the tariff in TRD-03?
feedback: The two $50-thousand distortion triangles sum to $100 thousand.

q: In TRD-03, consumer surplus falls from $1,250 thousand under free trade to $800 thousand after the tariff. The consumer loss is:
feedback: Consumer surplus falls by 1,250 − 800 = 450 thousand dollars.

q: In TRD-03, producer surplus rises from $50 thousand under free trade to $200 thousand after the tariff. The producer gain is:
feedback: Producer surplus rises by 200 − 50 = 150 thousand dollars.

q: Which welfare package correctly describes the tariff in TRD-03 relative to free trade?
options: Consumers lose $450k; producers gain $150k; government gets $200k; net welfare falls $100k
Consumers lose $200k; producers gain $200k; government gets $100k; net welfare rises $100k
Consumers lose $450k; producers gain $450k; government gets $200k; net welfare is unchanged
Consumers lose $100k; producers gain $150k; government gets $200k; net welfare rises $250k
feedback: The $450k consumer loss is only partly offset by the $150k producer gain and $200k tariff revenue, leaving $100k deadweight loss.

q: TRD-03 shows domestic production rising by 50 thousand and domestic consumption falling by 50 thousand after the tariff. What do those two changes represent?
options: Two transfers that exactly become government revenue
They are the two deadweight-loss distortions
A rise in comparative advantage and a fall in opportunity cost
Changes that leave total surplus unchanged
feedback: The tariff induces too much high-cost domestic production and too little domestic consumption relative to free trade.

q: Imports in TRD-03 fall from 200 thousand under free trade to 100 thousand after the tariff. Which statement is economically accurate?
options: The tariff raises both consumer surplus and total national surplus
The tariff eliminates imports without creating any distortion
The tariff protects domestic producers but reduces total national surplus
The tariff benefits consumers because domestic price rises
feedback: Protection increases domestic output, but the higher domestic price creates production and consumption distortions.

q: Checkpoint: Which complete quantity package is correct after the tariff in TRD-03?
options: Qs = 50 thousand; Qd = 250 thousand; imports = 200 thousand
Qs = 200 thousand; Qd = 100 thousand; exports = 100 thousand
Qs = 100 thousand; Qd = 200 thousand; imports = 100 thousand
feedback: At the tariff-inclusive price of $6, supply is 100 thousand and demand is 200 thousand, leaving 100 thousand imports.

q: In TRD-04, what domestic price results under the import quota?
feedback: The graph marks the domestic price under the quota at $6.

q: What world price is shown in TRD-04?
feedback: The green world-price line is drawn at $3.

q: At the quota-induced domestic price of $6 in TRD-04, domestic producers supply:
feedback: The $6 line intersects supply at Q = 150 thousand.

q: At the quota-induced domestic price of $6 in TRD-04, domestic consumers demand:
feedback: The $6 line intersects demand at Q = 200 thousand.

q: What import quantity is permitted by the quota shown in TRD-04?
feedback: At $6, imports equal Qd − Qs = 200 − 150 = 50 thousand.

q: What is the per-unit quota rent implied by TRD-04?
feedback: The domestic price is $6 while the world price is $3, creating a $3 price wedge per imported unit.

q: If domestic license holders receive the quota rents in TRD-04, total quota rents equal:
feedback: The $3 price wedge times 50 thousand imports produces $150 thousand in quota rents.

q: Free-trade imports at Pw = $3 would be 200 thousand. The quota cuts imports to 50 thousand. By how much do imports fall?
feedback: Imports fall from 275 − 75 = 200 thousand to 50 thousand, a decline of 150 thousand.

q: The quota raises domestic production from 75 thousand to 150 thousand. What is the production-distortion loss in TRD-04?
feedback: The production triangle is 1/2 × $3 × 75 thousand = $112.5 thousand.

q: The quota reduces domestic consumption from 275 thousand to 200 thousand. What is the consumption-distortion loss in TRD-04?
feedback: The consumption triangle is 1/2 × $3 × 75 thousand = $112.5 thousand.

q: Assuming quota rents remain domestic, what total deadweight loss is shown by TRD-04?
feedback: The two $112.5-thousand distortion triangles sum to $225 thousand.

q: In TRD-04, consumer surplus falls from $1,512.5 thousand under free trade to $800 thousand under the quota. The consumer loss is:
feedback: Consumer surplus falls by 1,512.5 − 800 = 712.5 thousand dollars.

q: Assuming domestic license holders receive the rents, which welfare package correctly describes TRD-04 relative to free trade?
options: Consumers lose $712.5k; producers gain $337.5k; quota rents are $150k; net welfare falls $225k
Consumers lose $337.5k; producers gain $712.5k; quota rents are $150k; net welfare rises $525k
Consumers lose $712.5k; producers gain $337.5k; quota rents are $375k; net welfare is unchanged
Consumers lose $225k; producers gain $150k; quota rents are $75k; net welfare is unchanged
feedback: The consumer loss exceeds the producer gain plus domestic quota rents by $225 thousand.

q: If the $150 thousand of quota rents in TRD-04 went to foreign exporters instead of domestic license holders, what would happen to domestic national welfare?
options: The national loss would be $150 thousand smaller
The national loss would be $150 thousand larger
Domestic national welfare would be unchanged
The quota would become a subsidy to consumers
feedback: Foreign capture of quota rents removes a transfer that otherwise remains inside the domestic economy.

q: TRD-04 raises domestic price from $3 to $6, expands domestic production, and reduces domestic consumption. Which interpretation is correct?
options: The quota raises efficiency because imports fall
The quota benefits consumers because domestic price rises
It protects producers but creates production and consumption distortions
The quota eliminates all welfare losses if rents are domestic
feedback: The quota moves production and consumption away from their free-trade levels, creating deadweight loss.

q: Checkpoint: Which complete quantity package is correct under the quota in TRD-04?
options: Qs = 75 thousand; Qd = 275 thousand; imports = 200 thousand
Qs = 200 thousand; Qd = 150 thousand; exports = 50 thousand
Qs = 150 thousand; Qd = 200 thousand; imports = 50 thousand
feedback: At the quota-induced price of $6, domestic supply is 150 thousand and demand is 200 thousand, leaving 50 thousand imports.
